meta.description: Science features, crater ages and located astrobiology findings for the lunar south pole.
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive; lon_east_180 (-180..180) and lon_east_360 (0..360). Where the notes gave only one form the other was computed during conversion (+/-360).
meta.validation: Copied from research notes of 2026-11-14. Not validated by the science lead.
source_meta_notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated.

Evidence labels (as in the notes): ESTABLISHED = measured / documented in primary or official sources; MODEL = result of a published simulation, not a measurement; CONTESTED = published but disputed; SPECULATIVE = hypothesis without supporting data. INTERPRETATION / PROPOSAL are used where the notes use them.

Item 'category' values: hazard_scarp, hazard_seismic, hazard_terrain, hazard_regolith, hazard_plume, hazard_dust, hazard_radiation, hazard_micrometeoroid, hazard_thermal, hazard_lighting, science_feature, crater_age, science_objective, geologic_product, astrobiology, planetary_protection, site_ranking.
There is NO evidence of indigenous lunar life. 'Possible bacteria' refers to forward contamination by terrestrial microbes (modelled dormant survival), not detection of lunar organisms.
No rule forbids landing in or near south-polar PSRs; Category IIb (south of 79 S) means documentation, not prohibition.
None of the published rankings is official; NASA has published no site scores.

properties.size: D 21.0 km, depth 4.2 km, floor 6.6 km
properties.age: Late Imbrian: rim 3.51 (+0.05/-0.08) Ga (Tye 2015); 3.60/3.69 Ga (Zuber 2012, flat floor/ejecta)
properties.science_value: Pole lies on its rim; PSR floor ~88-90 K; rim peaks sunlit ~80-90% of the time; >= 20 km3 impact melt; interior wall ~30 deg; rim blocks likely Shackleton ejecta that may expose SPA-related lithologies

items.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache Connecting Ridge (junction with Shackleton rim)

properties.age: Ancient ridge mantled by Shackleton ejecta
properties.science_value: 1:8,000 geomorphic map (Icarus 2022, pii S0019103522000835); ~8 m blocks near junction are primary sampling targets; flat spot with line of sight into Shackleton PSR; illumination 92.27-95.65% at 2-10 m, longest darkness 3-5 days
PSR pocket incl. possible CO2 cold trap; 2022 study of 'slope exposed ice'
Large PSR; coldest areas never exceed ~40 K

properties.size: D 50.9 km (52 km in Tye), depth 3.81 km
properties.science_value: H ~146 ppm (LP) / 220-245 ppm (LEND interp.); strongest, most uniform LAMP water-band signal of the four; possibly ~5%+ subsurface ice
664 km2 PSR (3rd largest); floor may hold ejecta from Imbrium, Orientale, Schrodinger; radar-bright signal probably rocks (ShadowCam)
Former VIPER site on west rim (Mons Mouton side); Griffin Mission One to land near Nobile with Astrolab FLIP rover
Near PSRs and extended illumination; IM-2 landed at -84.7906, 29.1958; IM-4 and Chang'e-8 planned for the plateau

properties.size: summit >5,000 m above base; ~3,500 m cliff
properties.age: 'Thought to be' SPA rim remnant (>4 Ga)
properties.science_value: Flat area near 86 S, 0 E is the heart of the candidate region; nearside slope faces Earth

items.name: Cabeus crater
items.limitations: Centre conflict: this note uses Wikipedia -84.9, -35.5; USGS Gazetteer list gives -85.33, -42.13 (see psr_and_ice.json).

properties.science_value: LCROSS ground truth (5.6 +/- 2.9 wt% water + other volatiles); impact at -84.6796, -48.7093
Volcanic vent (Schrodinger G) and lava flows; target of the Farside Seismic Suite

items.name: South Pole-Aitken basin
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED measurement; attribution to SPA is the authors' interpretation
items.limitations: No basin centre coordinates in notes.

properties.age: Chang'e-6 norite clasts: Pb-Pb 4247 +/- 5 Ma (interpreted as SPA impact, '4.25 Ga'); second event 3873 +/- 8 Ma (tentatively Apollo basin); crater-count model ages ~4.26-4.31 Ga; CE-6 landing site -41.625, -153.978
properties.science_value: Artemis sites targeted for PSR volatiles and ancient deposits related to SPA; Mons Mouton 'possibly' and Malapert 'thought to be' SPA rim remnants

items.name: Southernmost catalogued lunar pit: Schomberger A 1
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED for the catalogue; polar imaging hampered by lighting

properties.science_value: No listed pit lies poleward of 80 S (next are the Rutherfurd pits near -60.78); catalogue reported as 281 impact-melt, 15 mare, 5 highland pits. Natural-shelter credit should be zero poleward of 80 S (researcher inference).
Interpreted as extensive basin ejecta (Nature Communications 2024)

items.name: SPA material fraction at candidate regions (Gracy and Lee)

properties.science_value: Connecting Ridge 46% (rank 3 of 13); Peak Near Shackleton 47% (rank 2 of 13)

items.name: Non-ice resources at the south pole
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (orbital / Apollo-based); no in-situ measurement poleward of ~70 S

properties.science_value: Highland regolith > 40% O by mass, > 75% anorthite, iron-poor, < 2 vol% ilmenite; FeO differences within polar cap <= ~1 wt%; no Th/KREEP concentration; He-3 average ~4 ppb (unknown at pole); nearest bulk chemistry: Chandrayaan-3 APXS at 69.37 S, 32.32 E: Al2O3 26.1 wt%, FeO+MgO 14.4 wt%, Mg# 70; first in-situ sulfur detection (LIBS). Barely discriminates between south-polar sites.

items.limitations: Pre-Nectarian absolute ages 'particularly uncertain' (no sample calibration beyond ~3.9 Ga). Coordinates from Wikipedia. Lemelin 2021 lists model age 4.18 Ga.

items.name: Shackleton (Tye et al. 2015)
items.limitations: Zuber 2012: 3.60/3.69 Ga; water-ice note: 'crater 3.4-3.7 Ga'. Conflicting values kept.

items.name: Schuerger et al. 2019 Lunar Microbial Survival model (sunlit surface)

properties.finding: Sunlit external surfaces >100 C, up to 140 C at local noon; ~ -6 logs per 8 h at local noon; vacuum alone ~ -2 logs per 2107 days; deep internal surfaces ~ -0.02 logs per lunation; external surfaces unlikely to retain viable spores after one lunation.

items.name: Moores et al. 2025 (York Univ.): spore survival inside PSRs
items.limitations: The Shackleton/Faustini result is from Moores et al. 2025, NOT Saxena et al. (correction recorded in the notes).

properties.finding: Bacillus subtilis-type spores: reduction rates -0.0815 (Shackleton) and -0.0683 (Faustini) logs per lunation -> 30.0 yr and 30.8 yr to reach one Sterility Assurance Level (-12 logs); UV dominates for ~4-5 yr, vacuum thereafter; PSRs 'one of the least biocidal environments in the solar system'.

items.name: Saxena et al. 2026 (NASA Goddard/JSC, Science Advances, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aec0811)
items.evidence: MODEL (paper itself not retrieved; NASA release and news summary)

properties.finding: 'Survival' = alive >= 1 Earth day, not growth; Aspergillus niger most UV-resistant, max >= 7 days under optimal conditions; organisms: A. niger, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, Deinococcus radiodurans, Fusarium spp.; survivable niches range from a miles-wide crater floor to an astronaut boot print; robotic spacecraft can be baked >400 F (~204 C), crews cannot.
properties.locations: Nobile Rim, Connecting Ridge, de Gerlache Rim (Artemis candidate regions)
